title: Priming ramp thrash breadcrumbs
content:
Context:
Quick personal trail of what I tried when the dedicated GPU pool showed short, repeated drops in available capacity during midday traffic ramp. This is intentionally raw — breadcrumbing commands, partial logs, and hypotheses to share with infra/debug pairing later.

Symptom (summary):
- During steady traffic increase (11:30-12:15 PST) we observed repeated capacity thrash: pool size oscillated ±2-4 GPUs every ~3–7 minutes.
- Effect: increased tail latency for inference (p99 spike from 320ms -> 1.6s) and a spike in queued requests.
- Autoscaler reported both scale-out and scale-in actions in quick succession; some new pods failed readiness and then were evicted shortly after.

What I observed (timestamps local):
- 2026-03-05 11:28: autoscaler: scaleUp -> +4 gpus (requested), but controller logs show imagePull delays on 2 nodes.
- 2026-03-05 11:34: two nodes reported kubelet evicting pods: "eviction: memory pressure" on node gpupool-05.
- 2026-03-05 11:36: allocator: "failed to bind pod: insufficient allocatable gpus" even though cluster had transient free GPUs (race?).
- 2026-03-05 11:39: autoscaler scaleDown scheduled for some of the recently created nodes (age ~5m) — ended up removing a node that still had warm KV cache entries.

Commands and checks I ran (raw):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpupool   # check node readiness and age
- kubectl describe node gpupool-05  # saw memoryPressure conditions and kubelet evictionThreshold log snippet
- kubectl logs deployment/inference-router -n serving --since=20m | grep -i queue
- curl -s http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query?query=rate(kube_pod_status_phase{phase=\"Pending\"}[5m]) | jq
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="name~'gpupool'" --format="table(name,status,creationTimestamp)"
- ssh to node gpupool-07: docker ps -a | grep inference  # container startup stuck in Created state on two nodes

Notable log snippets (copied):
- "kubelet: eviction manager: node under memory pressure, attempting to evict pods to reclaim 1.3Gi"
- "dockerd: Error response from daemon: could not create shim task: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:...: device nvidia0 not found"
- "scheduler: binding rejected: insufficient gpuFree (requested 1, available 0)"
- "autoscaler: scaleDown: node gpupool-03 candidate (util 0.02) -> draining"

Hypotheses (ranked, quick):
1) Image pull / container runtime problems are delaying pod becomeReady; autoscaler interprets short-lived low-util nodes as underutilized and scales down too fast (policy mismatch: min-age too small).
2) Eviction thresholds too aggressive: system memory pressure on a few nodes (maybe host-side memory leak in nv-hostagent) leads to pod eviction that ripples into capacity calculations.
3) Race between allocator and autoscaler: allocator sees resources not yet reported as allocatable (kubelet not updated), so it fails bind; autoscaler then spins up more nodes, which themselves are not ready -> thrash.
4) KV cache priming loss: when nodes are removed quickly we lose warm caches; sudden traffic returning causes more requests to backpressure system and triggers new scale events (feedback loop).
5) Preemption / reclaim events from other clusters or housekeeping jobs stealing GPUs (low probability, but saw occasional 'preemption' tag in kube events).

Quick experiments to reproduce / validate:
- Increase node minAge (scaleDownDelay) to 10m in a staging pool and run synthetic ramp (ab) to see if thrash reduces.
- Force a delayed readiness on a node (simulate large image pull) and watch autoscaler behavior: does it add then remove too quickly?
- Turn off node auto-eviction (raise memory thresholds) in a test cluster to see if we remove eviction as a cause.
- Add more granular metrics: track node allocatable_gpu metric export and chart it at 10s granularity to spot lag between kublet and scheduler views.

Commands to run next (playbook draft):
- kubectl annotate deployment/inference-router redwood/debug-throttle=true -n serving  # route small test traffic only
- kubectl patch hpa/gpu-autoscaler -n infra --type=json -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/scaleDownDelaySeconds","value":600} ]'  # staging change
- PROMQ: rate(kube_node_status_allocatable{resource=\"nvidia.com/gpu\"}[30s]) and compare with kube_pod_spec_containers_resource_limits_gpu allocations
- Capture docker events on node during next spike: sudo journalctl -u docker -f > /tmp/docker-stream.log &

Things I want from infra folks / owners:
- Confirm if recent nv-hostagent daemon update rolled to gpupool-* around 2026-03-04 – correlates with first signs.
- Share any cluster maintenance or backup/cron jobs that might touch GPUs at midday.
- Review current scaleDown minAge policy for dedicated pools (we may want to bias toward "don’t remove nodes with < 10m age unless forced").

Misc notes and oddities:
- I saw a brief spike in pod Pending that matched a transient Prom API timeout at 11:31 — could be a monitoring blind spot causing misinformed scaling decisions.
- Some nodes (gpupool-02) report available gpu count but device nodes missing (/dev/nvidia0 absent) -> suggests kernel driver reload or device plugin crash.
- One failed pod showed stack: "cudaInit: CUDA driver version mismatch" — maybe mismatched driver/container combinations on new instances.

Next steps (my plan):
1) Run the controlled ramp in staging with scaleDownDelay bumped and high-resolution allocatable metrics capture.
2) Reproduce container runtime failure locally by simulating driver mismatch in a VM image.
3) Coordinate with infra to freeze nv-hostagent rollouts during traffic windows until we understand.
4) Draft a short mitigation: increase min node age + add "drain-protection" label to nodes with kv-cache warmed for a short TTL (30m) to avoid immediate removal.

Open questions for pairing session:
- How does the autoscaler compute candidate nodes for scaleDown when multiple nodes are similar util? (tie-break rules)
- Is there a central "priming score" telemetry anywhere for caches (KV cache hit rate by node) — would be handy to avoid removing valuable nodes instantly.
- Are there any sidecar init containers that might prolong readiness and are ignored by our readiness probe?

Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight, convert to a GitHub issue with reproducible steps once I have the staging run data. If we find driver/container mismatch, escalate to infra image owners (ami-build-team).

End of breadcrumbs.
